title: Serverless Event-Driven Order Processing Backend with AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS & LocalStack
problem: Traditional monolithic servers running continuously for variable or seasonal business workloads waste thousands of dollars in idle cloud compute costs, require complex auto-scaling group management, and suffer from single-point-of-failure bottlenecks during sudden traffic spikes. Naive serverless deployments experience crippling cold-start latency spikes, duplicate transaction executions from unhandled SQS retries, and silent message loss when downstream APIs fail. This project builds a production-grade serverless event-driven order processing backend in Python. The system deploys AWS Lambda functions emulated entirely on LocalStack, ingests order submissions via API Gateway, buffers asynchronous transactional workflows through Amazon SQS with Dead Letter Queues (DLQ), enforces idempotent ACID order state updates in Amazon DynamoDB, and achieves sub-100ms execution latency with zero external cloud expenses.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Flash-Sale Order Intake & Inventory Decrement
use_cases.first_sentence: Retail web applications processing sudden flash-sale traffic spikes need to accept thousands of order submissions without web server crashes.
use_cases.second_sentence: API Gateway immediately buffers orders into an SQS queue, returning a tracking ID to the buyer, while Lambda workers process inventory decrements asynchronously.

use_cases.title: Subscription Billing Webhook Processing Pipeline
use_cases.first_sentence: SaaS platforms receiving third-party payment gateway webhooks (e.g. Stripe, PayPal) need resilient ingestion that survives intermittent backend outages.
use_cases.second_sentence: Lambda functions validate webhook signatures and queue events to SQS; DLQs isolate failing webhooks for automated retry without dropping payment events.

use_cases.title: IoT Telemetry Batch Processing & State Storage
use_cases.first_sentence: Smart building sensor networks emitting periodic temperature and energy telemetry require scalable serverless ingestion that scales to zero overnight.
use_cases.second_sentence: Incoming telemetry bursts buffer through SQS and trigger batch Lambda executions, writing summarized device readings to DynamoDB with automated TTL expiry.

hard_parts: Configuring LocalStack container environments to emulate AWS Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, and DynamoDB with 100% API fidelity
Designing idempotent Lambda handlers using DynamoDB conditional writes (`attribute_not_exists`) to prevent duplicate charge transactions from SQS at-least-once delivery
Implementing exponential backoff retry policies and Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) redrive mechanisms to handle poison pill payloads cleanly
Optimizing Python Lambda function packaging and cold-start execution latency to achieve sub-100ms warm invocation durations
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating Lambda entrypoint handlers, SQS queue publishers, DynamoDB data access layers, and LocalStack deployment scripts
High-throughput benchmark report proving sustained processing of 1,000 asynchronous orders per minute with sub-100ms Lambda execution latency
Anti-fake verification script publishing duplicate order messages with the same idempotency key and asserting DynamoDB rejects the duplicate with zero duplicate charges

architecture.data_flow: A client sends an order JSON via HTTP POST to API Gateway; API Gateway validates the schema and enqueues the message directly into Amazon SQS, returning an order receipt ID to the client in < 25ms; SQS triggers the Order Processing Lambda function in batches of 10 messages; the Lambda function extracts the idempotency key and executes a conditional PutItem on DynamoDB (`attribute_not_exists(order_id)`); if the order already exists, it ignores duplicate processing; if new, it writes the order with status 'CONFIRMED' and updates inventory; if an unhandled error occurs, SQS retries the message 3 times before moving the payload to the DLQ; clients query order status via a secondary API Gateway endpoint.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: DynamoDB conditional expressions (`attribute_not_exists(order_id)`) preventing duplicate transactions; SQS maxReceiveCount=3 bounding retries.

targets.input: 1,000 orders submitted at 50 requests per second to API Gateway endpoint
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, LocalStack 3+ in Docker, Python 3.11 runtime
targets.minimum_pass: p95 end-to-end order processing latency is < 250 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 end-to-end order processing latency is < 85 milliseconds
targets.report: Serverless order processing latency report and CloudWatch log timing trace

targets.method: Percentage of duplicate SQS messages with identical order IDs rejected without duplicate DynamoDB writes or multiple charges
targets.input: 100 duplicate order messages injected into SQS queue simulating network retries
targets.environment: LocalStack DynamoDB instance with conditional write checks enabled
targets.minimum_pass: 100 of 100 duplicate order messages detected with 0 duplicate records created in DynamoDB
targets.target: 100 of 100 duplicate order messages detected with 0 duplicate records created in DynamoDB
targets.report: Idempotency verification audit log and DynamoDB record count parity report

targets.metric: Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) Poison Pill Isolation
targets.method: Verification of automatic dead-letter queue routing for malformed payloads after 3 failed Lambda execution attempts
targets.input: 20 intentionally malformed order payloads with invalid payment tokens injected into primary SQS queue
targets.environment: SQS queue with maxReceiveCount=3 linked to dead-letter queue in LocalStack
targets.minimum_pass: 20 of 20 poison pill messages routed to DLQ with 0 impact on healthy message processing
targets.target: 20 of 20 poison pill messages routed to DLQ with 0 impact on healthy message processing
targets.report: DLQ isolation test audit log and SQS queue depth monitoring report

Understanding of serverless architecture principles (Lambda, API Gateway), NoSQL databases (DynamoDB), and message queues (SQS)

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU and local container bound cloud emulator software)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local LocalStack container and Python)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external AWS cloud accounts, credit cards, or paid service quotas required (runs 100% offline via LocalStack)
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (LocalStack 3+ container) and Python 3.11 with boto3
environment.fallback_path: Mock Python in-memory queues and dictionaries mimicking SQS and DynamoDB APIs if LocalStack container is unavailable

riskiest_component.name: Duplicate Transaction Execution Under SQS At-Least-Once Delivery Retries
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce strict conditional writes on DynamoDB using unique idempotency keys (`attribute_not_exists(order_id)`).
riskiest_component.fallback: Secondary DynamoDB idempotency ledger table tracking processed message IDs.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a serverless event-driven order processing backend in Python with AWS Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS, and LocalStack.
worksheet.q2: Target users: cloud infrastructure engineers, serverless backend developers, and platform architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: e-commerce flash-sale order intake, subscription billing webhook processing, and IoT telemetry batch processing.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: LocalStack offline emulation, DynamoDB conditional write idempotency, SQS DLQ redrive policies, and Lambda cold-start optimizations.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: Lambda handlers, LocalStack setup scripts, DynamoDB schemas, and synthetic order payloads. Synthetic data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU bound, $0 cost using Docker LocalStack. Zero AWS charges.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: duplicate order execution under SQS retries. Fallback: DynamoDB conditional writes with unique idempotency keys.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: synchronous Flask app pretending to be serverless. Anti-fake check 5 fires 5 concurrent identical order requests and verifies exactly 1 write.
worksheet.q10: Safe; synthetic customer IDs and simulated retail order line items only, zero personal data.
